title: French diocesan missals, batch 4 (lane B): original-book and scholarly-described book states

traditions.label: Toulouse diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Printed missals of the metropolitan church of Saint-Étienne, Toulouse, as attested by two directly inspected originals (1490 and 1774).
traditions.coverage_note: Two publication states are documented from original leaves. The 1501–1552 prints, the 1773/1774 catalogue pair, the 1832 missal and the date of adoption of the Roman Missal remain open; no component collation links the two states.

traditions.label: Soissons diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Soissons diocesan Mass books: the 1687 Roman Missal with Soissons proper and the 1745 Fitz-James missal.
traditions.coverage_note: A 1687 Roman-Missal-plus-proper state (description) and the 1745 Fitz-James missal (original) are documented. The 1516/1531 prints, the post-Tridentine Soissons missal and the 1852 Roman restoration act remain open.

traditions.label: Vienne diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Printed missals of the church and province of Vienne: a Lyon-printed missal of 1519/1520 (inspected original) and the 1782 provincial missal (described).
traditions.coverage_note: A 1519/1520 publication state (original) and the 1782 promulgation of the provincial missal (scholarly description) are documented. Inspected copies of the provincial missal, its reprints and the Roman restorations remain open.

traditions.label: Nantes diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Printed Nantes missals described at exact loci in Duine's 1906 bibliography of Breton liturgical books.
traditions.coverage_note: Two sixteenth-century publication states are documented from scholarly description; the 1482 print, the eighteenth-century Poitiers-type liturgy, the 1837 missal and the 1858 Roman adoption remain without inspected book evidence.

traditions.label: Rennes diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Printed Rennes missals described at exact loci in Duine 1906.
traditions.coverage_note: Four fifteenth/sixteenth-century publication states are documented from scholarly description. The eighteenth-century missals, the 1780 cathedral-only adoption of the Tours liturgy and the Roman adoption (1846 or 1848) remain unverified against books.

traditions.label: Vannes diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Printed Vannes missals of 1530 and 1535 as reported by Duine 1906.
traditions.coverage_note: One 1535 state is documented from La Borderie's transcribed title and colophon and Duine's description; the Paris-books phase and the Roman adoption are named gaps.

traditions.label: Léon (Saint-Pol-de-Léon) diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The 1526 Missale Leonense as described by Duine 1906.
traditions.coverage_note: One publication state is documented from scholarly description; later Léon books and the see's suppression in 1790/1801 are outside the evidence.

traditions.label: Sées diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Sées diocesan Mass book from the 1742 Néel de Christot missal, as stated by diocesan historians.
traditions.coverage_note: The 1500 Rouen print is documented from its original colophon and the 1742 missal from scholarship; the Roman phases are named gaps.

traditions.label: Thérouanne (Morinensis) diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Printed missals for the use of Thérouanne before the see's destruction in 1553 and partition in 1559.
traditions.coverage_note: Two publication states are documented from a descriptive bibliography. The route has a historical endpoint: the see was suppressed after 1553 and partitioned on 29 June 1559.

traditions.label: Saint-Omer diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Saint-Omer diocese (1559–1801) and its 1785 Missale Audomarense.
traditions.coverage_note: No documented or provisional state: only bibliographic listings were found.

traditions.label: Troyes diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Troyes diocesan Mass books from the late-fifteenth-century prints to the 1736 Bossuet missal, as described and documented by Lalore.
traditions.coverage_note: Five states are documented from Lalore's descriptions and reprinted mandates, including a Roman-Missal-plus-supplement state (1696). The 1830 supplement and the 1846/1847 Roman restoration are gaps.

traditions.label: Mâcon diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The printed Mâcon missal of 1532 as described in the 1883 Notes on the liturgical books of Autun, Chalon and Mâcon.
traditions.coverage_note: One publication state is documented from description. The catalogue's c.1494 Mâcon missal was not found in this source; the 1601 adoption of the Roman office and the post-1801 history under Autun are gaps.

traditions.label: Verdun diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Verdun missals of 1509 and 1554 as described in Verdun bibliographies.
traditions.coverage_note: Two sixteenth-century states are documented from description. The 1699, 1779 and 1829 entries and the 1862 Roman restoration remain without book evidence.

traditions.label: Meaux diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Meaux diocesan missals as recorded in Allou's chronicle of the bishops of Meaux.
traditions.coverage_note: Three states (1556, 1709, 1836) are documented and one (1642) is provisional, all from Allou's chronicle; the 1858 Roman adoption is recorded as a gap with its mandate date.

traditions.label: Noyon diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Noyon diocesan missal under Bishop Charles de Broglie, attested before 1774.
traditions.coverage_note: The 1631 missal (Legg's negative rubric observation) and the 1770 Broglie missal are provisional; earlier and later books are named gaps.

traditions.label: Sisteron diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Sisteron missal of 1785 under Bishop Louis-Jérôme de Suffren.
traditions.coverage_note: One publication state is documented from scholarship; the original and its mandate remain uninspected; the see was suppressed in 1790/1801.

traditions.label: Montauban diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Montauban diocesan missal from the 1779 mandement to the 1847 Roman restoration.
traditions.coverage_note: Only a provisional 1779 state, without an identified edition, rests on Daux's summary; the catalogue years conflict.

traditions.label: Rieux diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Rieux diocesan Mass book under Bishop Pierre-Joseph de Lastic.
traditions.coverage_note: The 1776 Missale Rivense is documented from its original title and front matter as the Paris missal issued for Rieux.

traditions.label: Nîmes diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The nineteenth-century Nîmes diocesan liturgy of Larèche (from 1827) to its replacement by the Roman.
traditions.coverage_note: One 1511 state is documented from the original (title, calendar, colophon); the 1827 liturgy change is provisional; the 1831 missal and the Roman replacement are named gaps.

traditions.label: Mende diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Mende diocesan Mass book; no stage could be supported.
traditions.coverage_note: Two states rest on scholarship (1766 colour rubrics; 1840 mandement and additions); the 1763 neo-Gallican change and the 1860 Roman restoration are dated in the gap row.

traditions.label: Périgueux diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Périgueux diocesan Mass book; no stage could be supported.
traditions.coverage_note: No documented or provisional state: only bibliographic or secondary statements were reachable.

traditions.label: Tours diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Tours diocesan Mass book.
traditions.coverage_note: One incunable state rests on a bibliographer's colophon quotation (1485); a collated sequence witness dated 1492–93 is provisional because its edition is unidentified; the 1784 missal and the 1859 Roman restoration are named gaps.

traditions.label: Saint-Martin of Tours (collegiate church) missal
traditions.scope: The printed missal for the use of the church of Saint-Martin at Tours, distinct from the Tours cathedral and diocesan books.
traditions.coverage_note: One 1529 state is documented as the sole source of an edited sequence; no other Saint-Martin book is examined.

traditions.label: Tarbes diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Tarbes diocesan Mass book; no stage could be supported.
traditions.coverage_note: No documented or provisional state: only bibliographic or secondary statements were reachable.

traditions.label: Tulle diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Tulle diocesan Mass book; no stage could be supported.
traditions.coverage_note: One 1777 state rests on Évenou's quotation of the mandate; the Roman restoration is a named gap with conflicting dates.

traditions.label: Pamiers diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Pamiers diocesan Mass book; no stage could be supported.
traditions.coverage_note: One 1782 state is documented from the original title and dated letter; the 1845 missal and the Roman restoration are named gaps.

traditions.label: Mirepoix diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Mirepoix diocesan Mass book; no stage could be supported.
traditions.coverage_note: A provisional 1753 state rests on a scholar's remark and a reported change to the Clermont rite; no original was reachable.

traditions.label: Saint-Papoul diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Saint-Papoul diocesan Mass book; no stage could be supported.
traditions.coverage_note: One 1774 state is documented from the original title and dated letter.

traditions.label: Sarlat diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Sarlat diocesan Mass book; no stage could be supported.
traditions.coverage_note: No documented or provisional state: only bibliographic or secondary statements were reachable.

traditions.label: Tarentaise diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Tarentaise diocesan Mass book; no stage could be supported.
traditions.coverage_note: One undated printed state, assigned to Lyon about 1520–1521, rests provisionally on collated sequence witnesses; its identity with the catalogue's undated BnF print, the doubtful 1486 date and the undated Roman adoption are named gaps.

traditions.label: Saintes diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Saintes diocesan Mass book; no stage could be supported.
traditions.coverage_note: One 1491 state rests on collated Analecta hymnica sequence witnesses; later books are named gaps.

stages.label: 1490 Toulouse missal (Kleblat)
stages.date_label: Printed Toulouse, colophon and prefatory letter both dated 24 July 1490
stages.scope: One identified 1490 printing, its prefatory chapter letter, colophon and a calendar leaf.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum sancti Stephani Tolosae, Toulouse 1490, BM Toulouse Inc. Toulouse 106
stages.summary: A printed letter in the name of Archbishop Pierre de Lion, the provost Pierre de Rosergio and the chapter says that solemn Masses were celebrated with much discord because manuscript missals were old, faulty or disordered. They therefore had a missal ordered according to the church's rite, corrected by a named canon, and printed by Stephanus Kleblat for distribution throughout the archdiocese, exhorting deans, priors, archpriests and rectors to provide copies and celebrate according to it. The colophon names the book as for the metropolitan church of Saint-Étienne and dates it 24 July 1490. The November calendar carries Toulouse saints: Papulus (3 November) and Saturninus as a double (29 November), the latter line ending with 'Vigilia', the vigil of St Andrew.

evidence.locus: Canvas 7, unnumbered preliminary leaf recto, letter 'Universis…'
evidence.claim: Archbishop, provost and chapter order a corrected missal according to the Toulouse rite, printed by Kleblat and commended to the clergy of the diocese; dated 24 July 1490.

evidence.locus: Canvas 613, provider label XVIIv, right column
evidence.claim: Colophon: book of the missal for the metropolitan church of Saint-Étienne, printed by Stephanus Kleblat, 24 July 1490; printer's mark; preceded by the Prosa pro mortuis.
Calendar includes Papulus (3 November) and Saturninus, double (29 November), followed on the same line by 'Vigilia' (the vigil of Andrew, 30 November).

stages.limitations: No prayer, Ordo or Canon text was read. The letter states a corrective purpose; it does not identify an exemplar or describe specific textual changes. Earlier manuscript Toulouse missals remain uncompared.
stages.reception: The letter exhorts the diocesan clergy to obtain and use the printed missal; it is an exhortation, and actual adoption is not established.

stages.label: 1774 Toulouse missal (Loménie de Brienne)
stages.date_label: Title dated 1774; archbishop's pastoral letter dated 29 October 1772 (4 Kal. Nov.)
stages.scope: One identified 1774 printing, its title and the archbishop's complete pastoral letter describing the edition's programme.
stages.witness_label: Missale Tolosanum, Toulouse 1774, Google Books rZCkXZ7X0VQC
stages.summary: The title names Archbishop Étienne-Charles de Loménie de Brienne's authority with chapter consent. His letter says the new missal was made to agree with his recently published breviary (same Gospels, collects and scriptural chant texts) while keeping the Latin rite and order. It describes the distribution of Gospel and Epistle readings, with at least three ferial Gospels each week (Monday, Wednesday and Friday), each paired with its own Epistle. It says that the old Toulouse missal already gave proper Gospels to Advent ferias except Saturday. Chant texts were largely adopted from French missals, especially the Paris missal. Most orations came from the ancient sacramentaries. Prefaces were added for Advent, Septuagesima, saints, Corpus Christi, the Dedication and Toulouse saints, with two prefaces for Stephen and Saturninus taken from the old Missale Gothicum. Old sequences were kept for Easter, Pentecost, Christmas and Corpus Christi, and the rest came from the Paris missal. A Mass for the King was added. The letter commands all churches, chapters, monasteries, convents, seminaries, colleges, communities, orders and priests bound to the Toulouse Office to use this missal and forbids others.

evidence.claim: Missale Tolosanum by Loménie de Brienne's authority with chapter consent; Toulouse, Bibliopolae Usuum Tolosanorum, 1774, with royal privilege.
Primary description of the edition's programme: conformity to the new breviary, Gospel/Epistle distribution, sources of chants, orations, prefaces and sequences, Missa pro Rege.

evidence.locus: PA8–PA9, letter printed pp. 8–9; RA1-PP14 Monitum
evidence.claim: Mandate with addressees and prohibition of other missals; dateline 4 Kal. Nov. 1772, signed and countersigned; Monitum lists marginal source sigla (Roman and Gallican sacramentaries, Ambrosian, Paris 1685/1705/1738, old Toulouse, new Reims, Lyon missals).

stages.limitations: The letter's account of change is a contemporary claim; no predecessor missal was collated. The 1772 letter date and the 1774 title date are distinct events. Whether this copy belongs to the same printing as the catalogue's 1773 entry is unresolved.
stages.reception: The letter commands all churches, chapters, monasteries, convents, seminaries, colleges, communities and orders of the diocese, and priests bound by law or custom to the Toulouse Office, to use this missal and forbids others. The printed command names its addressees; it does not establish uniform actual uptake, a first effective-use date or the duration of use.

stages.label: 1687 Roman Missal with Proprium Missalis Suessionensis
stages.date_label: Proper printed at Soissons (Hanisset), cum permissu, 1687 (as described)
stages.scope: A Roman-Missal state: a Roman Missal with a printed Soissons proper bound after it, as described by Leclercq de Laprairie.
stages.witness_label: Missale Romanum with Proprium Missalis Suessionensis, Soissons 1687 (Acy church and seminary copies)
stages.summary: Leclercq de Laprairie describes a Roman Missal at the church of Acy followed by a 'Proprium Missalis Suessionensis' printed at Soissons by Hanisset with permission in 1687, during a vacancy of the see; the seminary library had another copy. He says the liturgy given by Bishop de Bourlon was that prescribed by Pius V, keeping many local elements. Ledouble confirms that the missal appeared after Bourlon's death, in 1687.

evidence.claim: Roman Missal with Proprium Missalis Suessionensis, Soissons, Hanisset, 1687; Bourlon's liturgy that of Pius V with retained local elements.
The missal of Bourlon's liturgy appeared in 1687, after his death.

stages.limitations: Copies described, not viewed; the edition of the Roman Missal is not identified. The 1745 letter's report of churches forced to use the Roman Missal is consistent with this state but is a separate statement.
stages.reception: The described copies belonged to a parish church and the seminary; diocesan uptake is not established.

stages.label: 1745 Soissons missal (Fitz-James)
stages.date_label: Title dated 1745; episcopal letter dated Soissons, 6 January 1745
stages.scope: One identified 1745 printing, its title and the bishop's complete letter describing the edition.
stages.witness_label: Missale Suessionense, Paris 1745, BM Lyon SJ LB 030/68 (Numelyo; Google Books JWXbxJ1ccrQC)
stages.summary: Bishop François de Fitz-James issues the missal after his new breviary. He says that copies of the Soissons missal hardly survived, so almost all churches had been forced to use the Roman Missal, and that Soissons rites survived only orally and were mixed with Roman ones. Apart from the orations, the body of the missal is composed from Scripture. Proper Epistles and Gospels for Wednesdays and Fridays are presented as an old Soissons usage, found in older Soissons missals including one printed shortly after Trent. The Gospels are distributed so that all four evangelists are read in a year. Orations come mostly from ancient sacramentaries, and a few prefaces were added (for example Advent and principal feasts). Lapsed rites common to neighbouring churches of the Reims province were restored, following Sixtus V's principle. All churches, chapters, pastors, monasteries, colleges, communities, sodalities and priests bound to the Soissons Office must use this missal; other missals and rites are forbidden.

evidence.claim: Missale Suessionense by Fitz-James's authority with chapter consent; Paris, J.-B. Coignard, 1745, royal privilege.
Primary description: prior forced use of the Roman Missal for want of Soissons copies; scriptural composition; Wednesday/Friday lessons; sacramentary orations; added prefaces; restored rites.
Mandate to the named institutions and priests; prohibition of other missals and rites; dated Soissons, 6 January 1745.

stages.limitations: The letter's comparison with earlier practice is a contemporary claim; no earlier Soissons missal or Roman Missal was collated. The post-Tridentine Soissons edition it mentions is unidentified.
stages.reception: The letter commands all churches, chapters, pastors, monasteries, colleges, communities, sodalities and priests bound to the Soissons Office. The printed command names its addressees; it does not establish uniform actual uptake, a first effective-use date or the duration of use.

stages.label: 1782 Vienne provincial missal (Lefranc de Pompignan)
stages.date_label: Pastoral letter dated 18 August 1782 promulgating the missal and breviary; publication reported as 1783; catalogue year 1784
stages.scope: The promulgation of a common missal and breviary for the province of Vienne, as described from the pastoral letter by the 1849 survey and by Pompignan's biographer.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum provinciae Viennensis (catalogue year 1784)
stages.summary: The 1849 survey describes Archbishop Lefranc de Pompignan's pastoral letter of 18 August 1782. It is addressed to the clergy of Vienne and, with the comprovincial bishops' consent, to the clergy of each diocese of the province, and it promulgates the new missal and breviary together. The author says Pompignan replaced the earlier Villars liturgy by adopting the Paris books of Vintimille, Viger and Mésenguy with some cuts, additions and corrections, after the provincial assembly of 1775. Pompignan's 1903 biographer notes that the breviary and missal were published in 1783 at Grenoble by the widow Giroud, with a Latin preface on the wish for books common to the province.

evidence.claim: Pastoral letter of 18 August 1782 promulgating the provincial missal and breviary; Paris-model books with corrections; 1775 provincial assembly.
Breviary and missal published 1783, Grenoble, widow Giroud, with a Latin preface on common provincial books.

stages.limitations: The letter was not viewed; its content is reported by a polemical survey. Publication is reported as 1783, while the catalogue witness is dated 1784; edition identity with the witness is assumed, not verified. The extent of dependence on the Paris missal is the author's judgement, not a collation.
stages.reception: The letter addresses the clergy of the whole province with the suffragans' consent; actual uptake in Grenoble, Valence, Viviers and Die is not established.

stages.label: 1519/1520 Vienne missal (Lescuyer, Lyon)
stages.date_label: Colophon: printed at Lyon, last day of February 1519 (possibly 1520 new style)
stages.scope: One identified Lyon printing for the use of Vienne: title, colophon and a calendar leaf.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum sancte Viennensis ecclesie, Lyon 1519, BM Lyon (Numelyo)
stages.summary: The colophon calls it the missal for the use of the holy church of Vienne, with very many offices newly added, printed at Lyon by Bernard Lescuyer on the last day of February 1519. The February calendar lists the Vienne bishops Avitus (5 February) and Simplicius (11 February), and Paschasius (22 February), with folio references to the sanctoral.

evidence.claim: Red title: missal for the use of the holy church of Vienne; Lyon library stamp.
Missal for the use of Vienne, with offices newly added; printed at Lyon by Bernard Lescuyer, last day of February 1519.
Calendar entries for Avitus and Simplicius, bishops of Vienne, and Paschasius, with sanctoral folio references.

stages.limitations: The phrase 'offices newly added' names no specific Masses, and no earlier Vienne missal was compared. No bishop's mandate was seen. The date bounds cover the year-style uncertainty, not a duration.
stages.reception: The title and colophon designate Vienne use; actual diocesan adoption is not established.

stages.label: 1520 Nantes missal (Rouen, Martin Morin)
stages.date_label: 1520 printing, as described by Duine from BnF Rés. B.1814
stages.scope: One identified 1520 printing (quarto, Rouen, Martin Morin) and one contents observation reported by Duine.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum insignis ecclesie Nannetensis, Rouen 1520 (Duine no. 46; BnF Rés. B.1814)
stages.summary: Duine describes the BnF copy as a quarto printed at Rouen by Martin Morin. At fol. CIII, after the ordinary Gloria, it has the Marian-farced 'Gloria de beata Maria', which Duine notes is not peculiar to Breton use.

evidence.claim: 1520 Nantes missal, Rouen, Martin Morin, BnF Rés. B.1814; second Gloria de beata Maria at fol. CIII.

stages.limitations: Scholarly description only; the original was not viewed. Copy identity with the USUARIUM 1520 record is assumed at edition level, not verified.
stages.reception: The title designates Nantes use; actual adoption is not established.

stages.label: 1588 Nantes missal (Philippe du Bec)
stages.date_label: 1588 printing at Nantes (Vincent Hucet), title transcribed by Duine
stages.scope: One identified 1588 printing whose transcribed title states episcopal mandate and approximation to the Tridentine exemplar.
stages.witness_label: Missale secundum usum insignis ecclesie Nanetensis, Nantes 1588 (Duine no. 47; BM Nantes 1277)
stages.summary: Duine transcribes the title of the Nantes municipal library copy. It was issued by mandate of Bishop Philippe du Bec, as approaching nearest to the Tridentine exemplar ('Ad exemplar Tridentinum proxime accedens'), and recently emended by men delegated in the Nantes synod. It was printed at Nantes by Vincent Hucet with royal privilege in 1588: a folio in roman type, in two columns.

evidence.claim: Title transcription: du Bec mandate, approximation to the Tridentine exemplar, synodal emendation; Nantes, Vincent Hucet, 1588.

stages.limitations: The title's claim of approximation to the Tridentine missal is the book's self-description reported by Duine; the extent of conformity to the 1570 Roman Missal is not collated. Duine's section heading prints the year ambiguously; the transcribed title ends 1588.
stages.reception: The title records episcopal mandate and synodal delegation; actual diocesan uptake is not established.

stages.label: 1492 Rennes missal (Michel Guibé)
stages.date_label: Colophon: finished at Paris, 10 January 1492 (as quoted by Duine); year style not stated, so possibly January 1493 by modern reckoning
stages.scope: One identified printing whose colophon, quoted by Duine, states episcopal correction.
stages.witness_label: Missale ecclesie Redonensis, Paris, colophon 10 January 1492 (Duine no. 10; BnF Vélins 201 = catalogue witness 7428)
stages.summary: Duine quotes the colophon. The missal and ordinary of the Mass, with the church's constitutions and customs added, omissions supplied and errors emended, was prepared by order of Bishop Michel Guibé through four named clergy and printed at Paris at the cost of the booksellers André Hodian and Jean Alexandre. It was finished on 10 January 1492.

evidence.claim: Colophon quoted: correction by order of Bishop Michel Guibé; Paris; finished 10 January 1492.

stages.limitations: Duine does not say whether the January date follows a year beginning at Easter; the bounds 1492–1493 express that year-style uncertainty, not a duration. Original not viewed; the described BnF copy is the holding of catalogue witness 7428, whose own age field is malformed.
stages.reception: The colophon records episcopal commission; actual adoption is not established.

stages.label: 1523 Rennes missal (Yves Mahyeuc)
stages.date_label: 1523 printing at Paris (Jean de Kerbriant), as described by Duine
stages.scope: One identified printing with its title, final-page statement of episcopal correction and approval, and added Masses.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad consuetudinem insignis ecclesie Redonensis, Paris 1523 (Duine no. 12; Arsenal 2742)
stages.summary: Duine quotes the title, which mentions the church's institutions and customs. He reports from the last page that the missal was corrected by order of Bishop Yves Mahyeuc and approved by him. It gained Masses of Our Lady of Pity, St Roch, St Claude and the Holy Name, and was printed at Paris by Jean de Kerbriant, alias Huguelin, in 1523.

evidence.claim: Title; correction by order of and approval by Bishop Yves; added Masses of Our Lady of Pity, Roch, Claude, Holy Name; Paris, Kerbriant, 1523.

stages.limitations: Duine paraphrases the final page; the added Masses are reported, not collated against 1492. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Episcopal approval is reported; actual uptake is not established.

stages.label: 1531 Rennes missal (Caen)
stages.date_label: Title imprint 1531, printed at Caen (as described by Duine)
stages.scope: One identified printing with its title and Duine's contents remarks on the Order of Mass.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum insignis ecclesie Redonensis, 1531 (Duine no. 13)
stages.summary: The title, as transcribed, says the missal was skilfully emended with several additions and newly joined Masses; Duine lists the Holy Name, Lacryma Christi, Visitation, Roch, Genevieve and Martha. He notes farced Kyries and two Glorias. He also notes that the Mass ends with the Placeat, without a final blessing or last Gospel.

evidence.locus: PA41 and PA43, printed pp. 41, 43, no. 13
evidence.claim: Title with added Masses and 1531 imprint, Caen; contents remarks on Kyries, Glorias and the ending of the Mass.

La Borderie transcribes the title ('Missale ad usum insignis ecclesie Redonensis, nuper ... emendatum ... Ex caracteribus Parrhisiis M.D.XXXI') and the last-leaf subscription naming Michel and Gérard Anger and Jacques Berthelot of Caen; he says the volume reproduces faithfully, with rare variants but some important additions, the Rennes missal text reformed in 1493 (BnF vellum copy).

stages.limitations: No bishop is named. Duine's remark that the Mass ends at the Placeat is his observation of one copy. The 1533 entry may be a second issue of this edition (Duine against Delisle).
stages.reception: Title designates Rennes use; uptake not established.

stages.label: 1588 Rennes missal (Aymar Hennequin)
stages.date_label: 1588 printing at Rennes (Pierre Bretel), title transcribed by Duine
stages.scope: One identified printing whose title states restoration and emendation by episcopal order with chapter consent.
stages.witness_label: Missale insignis ecclesiae Rhedonensis, Rennes 1588 (Duine no. 16)
stages.summary: Duine transcribes the title of the Grand Séminaire copy. It was restored and emended by order of Bishop Aymar Hennequin with the chapter's consent, and printed at Rennes by Pierre Bretel in 1588 with royal privilege. The sequences are gathered at the end, to be said or omitted at the celebrant's choice. The Ordinarium Missae offers an alternative litany-form Kyrie in three forms (fol. 159v–160r).

evidence.claim: Title with Hennequin order and chapter consent, Rennes 1588; sequences gathered at the end as optional; Kyrie alternatives fol. 159v–160r.

stages.limitations: Original not viewed; not among the Amiet-table witnesses. No claim of Roman conformity is made by the transcribed title.
stages.reception: Episcopal order with chapter consent is recorded; uptake not established.

stages.label: 1535 Vannes missal (Paris, Yolande Bonhomme)
stages.date_label: Colophon: 10 December 1535 (transcribed by La Borderie, 1891)
stages.scope: One identified printing: title and colophon as transcribed verbatim by La Borderie, with Duine's printing facts and contents report.
stages.witness_label: Missel vannetais de 1535 (Duine no. 53; Vannes episcopal library)
stages.summary: La Borderie transcribes the title, which calls the book newly emended with many added offices, and the colophon at the foot of fol. 236v. It was printed at Paris by Yolande Bonhomme, widow of Thielman Kerver, for Antoine and Michel les Papolins of Nantes and Guillaume Brunel of the Vannes diocese, on 10 December 1535; he describes a small folio of 240 leaves. Duine reports a copy in the Vannes episcopal library. An old manuscript note in the 1589 breviary, quoted by Duine, says that this missal gave St Denis a sequence and Credo for the whole diocese.

evidence.claim: Printing facts for the 1535 Vannes missal and a quoted manuscript note on its St Denis sequence and Credo.

Verbatim title ('Missale secundum usum insignis ecclesie Venetensis ... noviter emendatum ... cum multiplicibus divinis officiis superadditis') and colophon (Paris, Yolande Bonhomme, 10 December 1535); 240 leaves.

stages.limitations: Documented from scholarly transcriptions of the title and colophon (La Borderie) and a printing description (Duine); the original was not viewed by this lane. The contents claim about St Denis is second-hand through a manuscript note.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1526 Léon missal (Paris, Nicolas Prévost)
stages.date_label: 1526 printing at Paris, per the last leaf as reported by Duine
stages.scope: One identified printing, its last-leaf statement and Order-of-Mass remarks reported by Duine.
stages.witness_label: Missale Leonense, Paris 1526: edition described by Duine no. 63 (he names copies at the BnF, Rés. B.27804, and the Quimper Grand Séminaire); catalogue witness 6499 is the Quimper diocesan-library holding, matched at edition level
stages.summary: Duine reports from the last leaf that the missal was printed in 1526 at Paris by Nicolas Prévost at the cost of Yves Quilleveré. He quotes the phrase 'prefateque ecclesie ritui adaptatum', which he interprets as adapting the Léon liturgy to the Paris liturgy. He notes a Confiteor that does not copy the Roman formula, two different Glorias and farced Kyries.

evidence.claim: Printing facts from the last leaf; quoted adaptation phrase; Confiteor, Gloria and Kyrie remarks.

stages.limitations: The quoted Latin phrase literally refers to the rite of 'the aforesaid church'; Duine's reading of it as Paris use is his interpretation and is not adopted here. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1500 Sées missal (Rouen, for Pierre Regnault)
stages.date_label: Colophon: 1500, day 10 of an unnamed month (read on the original)
stages.scope: One identified printing: colophon and calendar openings of the Sainte-Geneviève copy.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum ecclesie Sagiensis, Rouen 1500 (BSG OEXV 486 RES)
stages.summary: The colophon says that the missal for the use of the church of Sées, newly corrected and emended ('de novo correctum et emendatum'), was printed at Rouen in the shop of Pierre Regnault, bookseller of the University of Caen, in 1500, on the tenth day of a month left blank. It follows rubrics on defects in the celebration of Mass. The calendar runs from January.

evidence.claim: Missal for Sées use, 'de novo correctum et emendatum', printed at Rouen in Pierre Regnault's shop, 1500, 'die x mensis' with the month blank.
Printed calendar from January to April.

stages.limitations: The colophon names no bishop. The claim to be newly corrected is the book's own; no predecessor (1488 or 1496) was compared. The copy is incomplete.
stages.reception: Title designates Sées use; uptake not established.

stages.label: 1742 Sées missal (Néel de Christot)
stages.date_label: Missal printed 1742 (Hommey); mandate date not given
stages.scope: The fact, date and episcopal authorship of the 1742 Sées missal, and its stated relation to the diocesan breviaries, as reported by Hommey.
stages.witness_label: Missale Sagiense, 1742 (Néel de Christot)
stages.summary: Hommey says Bishop Néel de Christot completed Jacques Lallemant's liturgy and promulgated its missal and ritual. He adds that the missal, printed in 1742, and Néel de Christot's 1745 breviary did not agree with Lallemant's breviary. Marais and Beaudouin date Lallemant's breviary mandement to 15 August 1737 and say that the Roman breviary had been in use at Sées for over a century before it.

evidence.locus: PA56 and PA409, printed pp. 56 and 409
evidence.claim: Néel de Christot promulgated the missal completing Lallemant's liturgy; missal printed 1742; disagreement with Lallemant's breviary.

evidence.locus: PA217 and PA220, printed pp. 217 and 220
evidence.claim: Lallemant's new breviary promulgated by mandement of 15 August 1737 after more than a century of Roman breviary use.

stages.limitations: No original page or mandate text was viewed; the content of the missal is not described beyond its relation to the breviaries.
stages.reception: Promulgation is stated; actual uptake is not established.

stages.label: 1516 Thérouanne missal (Rouen, Martin Morin)
stages.date_label: Final note: 12 November 1516 (as reported in French by the bibliography)

stages.label: 1736 Troyes missal (Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet)
stages.date_label: First mandate 16 September 1735; publication mandate 26 September 1736
stages.scope: The 1736 Bossuet missal, its two mandates and the documented controversy and correction mandate.
stages.witness_label: Missale Trecense, Troyes 1736 (Bossuet)
stages.summary: Lalore prints Bishop Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet's Latin mandate of 16 September 1735 and his French mandate of 26 September 1736. The latter presents the missal as made to answer the new breviary, prepared by learned men chosen with the chapter, and as the awaited replacement for the foreign missals whose use his predecessors had tolerated; Lalore's chronology (p. 111) records it as making the new missal obligatory. Lalore's chronology records a royal commission under Cardinal de Rohan, a Conseil d'État arrêt of 11 June 1737, and Bossuet's fourth pastoral instruction and ordinance of 15 October 1738, in which he retracted several provisions of the missal and restored the former rubrics on three principal points (pp. 112, 117).

evidence.claim: Mandates of 16 September 1735 and 26 September 1736 for the new Troyes missal.
Controversy chronology: Rohan commission, arrêt of 11 June 1737, and the 15 October 1738 instruction and ordinance retracting several provisions and restoring former rubrics on three points.

stages.limitations: The ordered corrections of 1738 imply a corrected state whose printed form was not seen; no collation with the Roman Missal or the 1580 book. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: The 1736 mandate orders use by the diocese; the controversy shows contested reception; uptake not established.

Reprint by Psaulme dated 1557.

stages.date_label: Missal appeared 1836 (Allou); breviary 1834

stages.witness_label: Missale Meldense, 1836
stages.summary: Allou says that because the Meaux books were running out, the Paris breviary and missal were adopted provisionally for the cathedral in 1824. Bishop Gallard then gave the diocese a new liturgy, with breviary offices following Paris and the rest by Canon Pruneau. The breviary appeared in 1834 and Pruneau's missal in 1836. The 1849 survey confirms the 1834 Pruneau liturgy and lists Meaux as having its own liturgy.

evidence.claim: 1824 provisional Paris books for the cathedral; Gallard's new liturgy; breviary 1834, Pruneau's missal 1836.
1834 Pruneau liturgy; table entry 'de Meaux'.

stages.limitations: Contents not described; the 1845 reissue was not found. Original not viewed.

stages.label: 1631 Noyon missal (Noyon, Michel and Claude Sonnius)
stages.date_label: 1631 as given by Legg; 15 March 1631, Noyon, by Weale–Bohatta (title leaf not inspected)
stages.scope: Existence of a 1631 Noyon missal that one scholar examined; no positive content is reported.
stages.witness_label: Missale Noviomense, Noyon, Michel and Claude Sonnius, 1631 (Weale–Bohatta no. 683)
stages.summary: Legg says he examined the Noyon missal of 1631 and did not find directions for mixing the chalice at any time; he contrasts it with the Broglie missal of 1770, which prescribes the preparation during the Kyrie. His remark that the elements would seem to be ready prepared at the offertory anthem is his inference from that absence, not a rubric of the book. Weale–Bohatta give the imprint: Noyon, Michel and Claude Sonnius, 15 March 1631.

evidence.claim: 'I have examined the Missal of 1631': Legg found no directions for the mixing at any time (a negative observation; his 'ready prepared' remark is an inference from it).
1631, 15 Mar., Missale Noviomense, Noyon, sumptibus Michaelis et Claudii Sonnius; folio; copies Amiens, London BM.

stages.limitations: Cold review 2026-10-22: provisional. The only inspected evidence about the book is Legg's negative observation, which shows nothing positive about its contents and does not prove that the book lacked such a direction; Legg identifies the book by year only, and its title, printer and date come from the Weale–Bohatta entry (bibliographic level). No title leaf, colophon or mandate was inspected. Whether this missal is Roman with a Noyon proper (Ledouble's post-1583 reintroduction) is not stated by either source.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: Noyon missal of Charles de Broglie (attested by 1774)
stages.date_label: Attested by derivative books of 1774 and 1777; no printing year given
stages.scope: Existence of a Broglie missal, attested by its recorded title and by lay books that follow it.
stages.witness_label: Missale Noviomense (Charles de Broglie)
stages.summary: The Bibliographie noyonnaise records the title of a Missale Noviomense issued by Bishop Charles de Broglie's authority with chapter consent, known through a 1780 chapter memoir. It lists a 1774 Eucologe and 1777 Heures for Noyon that follow Bourzac's breviary and 'the missal printed by order of Mgr de Broglie'. Legg (1905) cites the book as 'Missale Noviomense (de Broglie episcopo) 1770' and reports its rubrics for preparing the chalice at high Mass, with internal loci.

evidence.claim: Broglie missal title; Eucologe 1774 and Heures 1777 following Bourzac's breviary and Broglie's missal.

Legg cites 'Missale Noviomense (de Broglie episcopo) 1770', Ritus in missa maiori, pars iii cap. iii and cap. vii (p. xliii): at high Mass the subdeacon brings the chalice during the Kyrie, the deacon pours the wine, the celebrant blesses the water, and the chalice goes to the credence until the offertory.
Missale ecclesiae Noviomensis, Paris, G. Desprez, folio; copies at Amiens and elsewhere (no year in the 1928 OCR line; Weale 1886 gives 1770).

stages.limitations: Provisional: no title leaf, colophon or mandate was inspected. Legg's citation gives the imprint year 1770 (matching the catalogue year) and two rubric loci, but not the title or mandate text, so the stage is not upgraded under this lane's rule. The 1774 attestation year is kept as the date of the derivative books.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1785 Sisteron missal (Suffren; Toulouse liturgy)
stages.date_label: Missale Sistaricense, Toulouse, Joseph Dalles, 1785 (cited imprint)
stages.scope: Existence, imprint and liturgical identity of the 1785 Sisteron missal as stated by Albanès.
stages.witness_label: Missale Sistaricense, Toulouse, Joseph Dalles, 1785
stages.summary: Albanès says Bishop Suffren introduced a new liturgy that had nothing of Sisteron but the name, being the Toulouse liturgy, even down to a proper preface for St Saturninus. Everything was printed at Toulouse: the breviary in 1778 and the missal seven years later, in 1785. His footnote cites the imprint: Missale Sistaricense, Toulouse, Joseph Dalles, 1785, quarto.

evidence.claim: Toulouse liturgy introduced under Suffren; breviary 1778; Missale Sistaricense, Toulouse, J. Dalles, 1785, in-4.

stages.limitations: The identification with the Toulouse liturgy is the historian's, citing contemporary opinion; no collation with the 1774 Toulouse missal. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1779 Montauban breviary-and-missal mandement
stages.date_label: Mandement dated 24 February 1779; obligatory from 28 November 1779 (Daux)
stages.scope: A mandated change of missal stated by Daux; no edition identified.
stages.witness_label: No exact edition identified
stages.summary: Daux reports a mandement of 24 February 1779 ordering in all churches the new breviary and missal of Montauban, with gradual and vesperal. The bishop says he chose, for uniformity with the metropolis, the breviary and missal already adopted by the other Toulouse suffragans, and their use became obligatory from 28 November 1779. Daux says the diocese was the last in France to take it.

evidence.claim: Mandement of 24 February 1779 ordering the new breviary and missal; obligatory from 28 November 1779.

stages.limitations: Provisional: no printed missal is identified. The catalogue's 1773 Missale Montalbanense and 1774 Missae pro defunctis predate this mandement, and the 1772 Nouvelles ecclésiastiques (cited in the 1849 survey) already lists Montauban among sees taking a Paris-type breviary. The conflict is unresolved.
stages.reception: Obligation from 28 November 1779 is stated; actual uptake not established.

stages.label: 1776 Rieux missal: the Paris missal issued for Rieux (Bishop de Lastic)
stages.date_label: Title-page imprint 1776 (read on the original); adoption reported in the Nouvelles ecclésiastiques of 6 March 1778 as made 'some time ago'
stages.scope: The title and front matter of the 1776 Missale Rivense, with the periodical's report of the change from the Roman books.
stages.witness_label: Missale Rivense, Paris 1776 (Toulouse university copy, Tolosana PPN164509542; catalogue witness 7439)
stages.summary: The title page names Bishop Pierre-Joseph de Lastic's authority and the chapter's consent and was printed at Paris for the booksellers of the Paris and Rieux uses in 1776. Its only prefatory letter is Archbishop Vintimille's letter to the Paris clergy dated 11 March 1738, which indicates that the book is the Paris missal issued for Rieux; the Mass texts were not compared. The Nouvelles ecclésiastiques of 6 March 1778 report that Lastic had replaced the Roman books still in use with the Paris breviary and missal, choosing the latest edition with the Sacred Heart office.

evidence.locus: RA1-PA37 (issue date) and RA1-PA39 ('De Rieux en Languedoc')
evidence.claim: Adoption of the Paris breviary and missal in place of the Roman books; Sacred Heart office in the chosen edition.
'Missale Rivense', authority of Bishop Pierre-Joseph de Lastic with the chapter's consent; Paris, for the booksellers of the Paris and Rieux uses; 1776.
Vintimille's letter 'Clero Parisiensi' dated Paris, 11 March 1738, is the book's prefatory letter; no Rieux letter precedes the table.

stages.limitations: Upgraded from provisional on the inspected title leaf. The front matter of one copy was read; the Mass texts were not collated against a Paris edition. The Nouvelles ecclésiastiques are a partisan periodical. The periodical names no edition: linking its report to this 1776 book is an inference from the title and front matter, and the Sacred Heart Mass it mentions was not checked in this copy.
stages.reception: The periodical reports chapter and clergy dissatisfaction; uptake is not established.

stages.label: 1511 Nîmes missal (Lyon, Jean Moylin)

Calendar entries 'Translatio sancti ferreoli' and 'Translatio sancti baudilii martyris'.

evidence.locus: Image n539 (colophon, after the last Mass for the dead)
evidence.claim: Missal for the priests of Nîmes; completed by Johannes Moilin alias de Cambray, Lyon bookseller, at his expense and at the bishop of Nîmes's command; dated 1511, 22 October.
1511, 22 Oct., Missale ecclesie Nemausensis, Lyon, Iohannes Moilin alias de Cambray; copies Aix, Nîmes, Paris S.G.

stages.label: 1827 Nîmes diocesan liturgy (Larèche)
stages.date_label: Change dated 1827 by the 1849 survey
stages.scope: A reported change from the Roman to a new diocesan liturgy; the missal is not described.

stages.summary: The 1849 survey says that in 1827 Nîmes left the Roman for an entirely new liturgy composed by the abbé Larèche, vicar general of Bishop de Chaffoy; its table lists Nîmes as having its own liturgy. Boucarut (1857) says the breviary and missal were given by Bishop de Chaffoy in 1826, adapted from the Besançon books, that the 1835 synod ordered Mass to be said according to the Missale Nemausense, and that the missal differed from the Roman only in its sung parts and some epistles, gospels and orations, keeping the Roman order, Canon and Ordinary.

evidence.claim: Nîmes left the Roman in 1827 for Larèche's new liturgy; table entry 'de Nîmes'.
Synod of 27–29 September 1851 decreed the replacement of the Nîmes liturgy by the Roman.

Missal and breviary of 1826 (Chaffoy), adapted from Besançon; 1835 synod's 'Missa autem secundum Missale Nemausense semper celebretur'; differences from the Roman confined to chants and some readings and orations.
Missale Nemausense, 1831: colours nearly Roman, except red in Passiontide, on Good Friday and on Holy Innocents.

stages.limitations: Provisional: no title leaf, colophon or mandate of the Nîmes missal was inspected, so the stage is not upgraded under this lane's rule. The sources date the new books 1826 (Boucarut), 1827 (the 1849 survey and Bergier) and 1831 (the catalogue and Legg's copy); the 1831 witness may be a later printing of the same liturgy.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.limitations: A one-word classification of the colour rubrics by a scholar who owned the book; no mandate or title text. Whether the 1766 missal follows the 1763 Paris-type breviary (Pascal, Gabalum christianum, 1853, pp. 154 and 266, as read by a lane helper) is not stated by Legg.

stages.scope: The printed missal as a collated witness of the sequence for St Gatian, first bishop of Tours.
stages.witness_label: No inventory witness linked: Analecta hymnica 40 siglum C of no. 214 ('Missale Turonense imp. Turonis. 1492–93'); catalogue witness 7611 (1493) probably represents the Rouen edition named in the limitations
stages.summary: Dreves edits the sequence 'Sancti Gatiani laudes' for St Gatian from a fifteenth-century Langres manuscript (Parma) and two printed Tours missals, of 1491 (B) and of Tours 1492–93 (C), recording readings of both.

evidence.claim: Witnesses B 'Missale Turonense imp. 1491' and C 'Missale Turonense imp. Turonis 1492–93', both collated.

stages.limitations: Cold review 2026-10-22: provisional; the exact book is not identified. Weale–Bohatta list no Tours-printed edition of 1492–93: their only 1493 Tours missal (no. 1595) was printed at Rouen by Martin Morin on 17 April 1493, with a copy at Tours, and cites Van Praet no. 366, a Sainte-Geneviève copy whose dominical-letter table begins in 1492. Analecta hymnica's 'imp. Turonis 1492–93' may describe that Rouen edition with a wrong place, or an edition not otherwise recorded. Catalogue witness 7611 (1493, BM Tours) most probably is the Rouen edition, so it is not linked. Attests one local sequence; the original was not viewed. The 1491 print (B) has no separate candidate here.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1529 Saint-Martin of Tours missal (Paris)
stages.date_label: 'imp. Parisiis 1529' as cited by Analecta hymnica (no leaf inspected)
stages.scope: The printed missal of Saint-Martin as the sole source of an edited sequence.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum ecclesie beatissimi Martini Turonensis, Paris 1529 (catalogue witness 7614; AH 39 no. 220)
stages.summary: Dreves edits the St Catherine sequence 'Ave, virgo generosa' (AH 39 no. 220) from the 1529 Paris-printed missal of St Martin of Tours as his only source, listing three readings he corrected.

evidence.claim: Sole source 'Missale B. Martini Turonensis imp. Parisiis 1529'.

stages.limitations: Attests one sequence. AH 54 (no. 163, p. 253) lists the same book as an uncollated witness of a Trinity sequence. The original was not viewed.
stages.reception: Designated for the church of St Martin; not established beyond it.

stages.label: 1777 Tulle missal (the Paris missal under a diocesan title)
stages.date_label: 1777 as given by Évenou; the mandate's own date is not quoted
stages.scope: The episcopal mandate printed at the head of the 1777 Missale Tutellense, as quoted by a modern scholar.
stages.witness_label: Missale Tutellense, 1777 (catalogue witness 7617)
stages.summary: Évenou quotes the mandate at the head of the 1777 Missale Tutellense: since the Paris missal had already been received by many churches of France, it should be held beyond reproach, and the bishop offers it to his clergy. He counts Tulle among the dioceses that adopted the Paris missal by giving it a diocesan title.

evidence.claim: Mandate at the head of the 1777 Missale Tutellense quoted ('Cum a pluribus Galliarum Ecclesiis Missale illud [Parisiense] jam fuerit admissum ...'); Tulle among dioceses that gave the Paris missal a diocesan title.

stages.limitations: Scholarly quotation of the mandate without its date or locus in the book; the original was not viewed. Which Paris edition was taken over is not stated.
stages.reception: The mandate offers the book to the clergy; uptake is not established.

stages.label: 1782 Pamiers missal (Bishop Henri-Gaston de Lévis)
stages.date_label: Title-page imprint 1782; pastoral letter dated Pamiers, 1 June 1781 (read on the original)
stages.scope: Title leaf and the bishop's prefatory letter of the Toulouse university copy.
stages.witness_label: Missale Appamiense, Paris, Claude Simon, 1782 (Tolosana PPN164509283; catalogue witness 6904)
stages.summary: The title names Bishop Henri-Gaston de Lévis's authority with the chapter's consent; Paris, Claude Simon, 1782. In his letter to the clergy the bishop says that, having issued a new breviary, he had a new missal made to agree with its offices, and that care was taken that nothing in the order or the Canon of the Mass was changed, keeping the norm the Roman Church observes, except that at one or two places, the Commemoration of the living and the prayer after the fraction of the Host, a reading from old sacramentaries and the province's old missals was restored for clarity. He orders all churches, monasteries, colleges and priests of the diocese to use it in solemn and private Masses and no other. The letter is dated at Pamiers on 1 June 1781.

evidence.claim: 'Missale Appamiense', Lévis's authority with chapter consent; Paris, Cl. Simon; 1782.

evidence.locus: Tolosana pages 11–15 (letter, printed pp. 3–7; date on page 15)
evidence.claim: New missal to agree with the new breviary; order and Canon kept unchanged except for a restored reading at the Commemoration of the living and at the prayer after the fraction (printed p. 6, Tolosana page 14); use mandated diocese-wide; dated 1 June 1781.

stages.limitations: Front matter of one copy; the Mass texts were not collated. Bergier (1860, p. 384, read by a lane helper) says Pamiers left the Pius V books in 1781.
stages.reception: The letter mandates exclusive use; uptake is not established.

stages.label: 1753 Mirepoix missal (Bishop de Champflour)
stages.date_label: 1753 as cited by Chevalier and Weale–Bohatta (title leaf not inspected)
stages.scope: Existence of the 1753 Missale Mirapicense, one contents remark and a reported change of rite.
stages.witness_label: Missale Mirapicense, Paris, Garnier and Le Prieur, 1753 (catalogue witness 5801)
stages.summary: Ulysse Chevalier remarks that a prose discussed in a book he reviews is found in the Missale Mirapicense of 1753. Bergier says Mirepoix took the Clermont rite in 1753.

evidence.claim: A prose 'se trouve naturellement dans le Missale Mirapicense (de 1753)'.

evidence.locus: pp. 12–13 and 384 (images n22–n23, n394; read by a lane helper)
evidence.claim: Mirepoix took the Clermont rite in 1753.

stages.limitations: Provisional: no title leaf, colophon or mandate of the missal was inspected, the prose is not named on the cited page, and the Clermont attribution is a secondary statement. The companion 1753 breviary's mandate (25 March 1753) dates the reform of the office, not the missal. The Gallica copy (bpt6k325514v) refused access.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1774 Saint-Papoul missal (Bishop Daniel-Bertrand de Langle)
stages.date_label: Title-page imprint 1774; pastoral letter dated 15 August 1773 (read on the original)
stages.scope: Title leaf and the bishop's prefatory letter of the Toulouse university copy.
stages.witness_label: Missale Sanpapulense, Toulouse 1774 (Tolosana PPN060318996; catalogue witness 7480)
stages.summary: The title names Bishop Daniel-Bertrand de Langle's authority with the chapter's consent; Toulouse, for the booksellers of the Saint-Papoul uses, 1774. His letter says that the missal completes the recently issued breviary. The introits, graduals, offertories and communions were all taken from Scripture, and the collects, secrets and postcommunions partly from the Roman and partly from the Paris missal, most of them from the Gregorian sacramentary. It is dated at Saint-Papoul on the Assumption, 15 August 1773.

evidence.claim: 'Missale Sanpapulense', Langle's authority with chapter consent; Toulouse; 1774.

evidence.locus: Tolosana pages 16–18 (letter, printed pp. 3–5; date on page 18)
evidence.claim: Missal completes the new breviary; chants from Scripture; orations partly Roman, partly Parisian; dated 15 August 1773.

stages.limitations: The letter's account of sources is the bishop's own; no Mass text was collated. A 1912 bibliography (Bull. Comm. archéol. Narbonne 12, p. 487 no. 2661) dates the book 1773, probably from the letter.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: Printed Tarentaise missal, undated (assigned to Lyon about 1520–1521 by Analecta hymnica)
stages.date_label: Undated print assigned to Lyon 1520 by Dreves; a Lyon 1521 edition cited elsewhere in Analecta hymnica (no leaf inspected)
stages.scope: The printed Tarentaise missal as a collated witness of a sequence for its own saint and of an Epiphany sequence.
stages.witness_label: No inventory witness linked: Analecta hymnica 44 siglum B of no. 167 ('imp. s. l. et a. [Lugduni 1520]') and AH 40 siglum D of no. 9 ('imp. Lugduni 1521'); possibly the undated BnF print catalogued as witness 7552 (identity unverified)
stages.summary: Dreves edits the sequence for St James of Tarentaise, 'Laudum praeconia' (AH 44 no. 167), from a fifteenth-century Tarentaise manuscript missal and the undated printed Tarentaise missal he assigns to Lyon, 1520. AH 40 collates a 'Missale Tharantasiense' printed at Lyon in 1521 for an Epiphany sequence.

evidence.claim: Witness B: 'Miss. Tharentasiense imp. s. l. et a. [Lugduni 1520]', collated against BnF lat. 8889.
Witness D: 'Miss. Tharantasiense imp. Lugduni 1521', collated.

stages.limitations: Cold review 2026-10-22: provisional and not linked to a witness. The print carries no place or date: Dreves supplies '[Lugduni 1520]' in brackets and AH 40 gives 'Lugduni 1521', so the exact book (place, printer, date) is not identified. Weale–Bohatta (no. 1525) list only one printed Tarentaise missal, an undated, incomplete BnF copy, and catalogue witness 7552 ('about 1486', BnF B-1484) is likewise an undated BnF print; both Analecta hymnica editions collate the print against BnF lat. 8889, so it may be that same book. Neither identity nor distinctness is established. The bounds 1520–1521 express the editors' attributed dates, not an inspected imprint; the original was not viewed. The catalogue's '1486 (about)' date is itself unconfirmed (see the gap row).
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1491 Saintes missal (Paris, Jean Higman)
stages.date_label: 1491 as cited by Analecta hymnica (title leaf not inspected)
stages.scope: The printed missal as a collated witness of two sequences.
stages.witness_label: Missale Xanctonense, Paris 1491 (Cambridge UL copy = catalogue witness 7657; Analecta hymnica 54 siglum B of no. 109 and F of no. 162)
stages.summary: Blume and Bannister collate the Paris 1491 Saintes missal as witness B of the Transfiguration sequence 'Haec est dies summe grata' (no. 109), with readings it shares with a fifteenth-century Saintes manuscript missal, and as witness F of a Trinity sequence (no. 162).

evidence.claim: 'Miss. Xantonense impr. Parisiis 1491' is witness B, collated; variants shared with the Saintes manuscript missal A (BL Lansdowne 450).
The same print is witness F of a Trinity sequence.

stages.limitations: Attests two sequences in the book. Weale and Misset's Analecta liturgica (pp. 236–247) list some fifty proses from the same print (heading and p. 237 viewed by a lane helper only). An undated Paris-type 'Missale Santonense' (BMC VIII 229–230, IA.41362) is a separate edition not covered here. The printer and day in the label (Jean Higman, 15 April 1491) come from Weale–Bohatta no. 1663, which records the Cambridge copy; Analecta hymnica gives only 'impr. Parisiis 1491'.
stages.reception: Not established.

gaps.missing: Original 1501, 1524, 1539, 1540 and 1552 prints; the 'old Toulouse missal' the 1772 letter compares, and its identity relative to the 1490 book; component collation of ferial Gospels, prefaces and sequences across the two states.
gaps.next_source: BM Toulouse Res. B XVI 277 (1501) and B.XVI.36/164 (1524) if digitised on Rosalis; Gallica copies when reachable; collate 1490 Advent ferial Gospels against the 1772 letter's claim.
gaps.consequence: Two publication states are recorded without a documented revision transition; the letter's before/after claim names no exact predecessor edition.

gaps.period: 1774 to the adoption of the Roman Missal
gaps.missing: The 1773 catalogue entry (identity with 1774), the 1832 Missale Tolosanum, and the dated act for the adoption of the Roman Missal. L'épiscopat français (1907, p. 626) says Archbishop Mioland prepared, and Archbishop Desprez carried out from 1861, the re-establishment of the Roman liturgy; the 1849 survey lists Toulouse as Parisian.
gaps.next_source: BnF B-934 (1832) and BL L.18.b.3; Desprez's Roman-liturgy mandement of c.1861.
gaps.consequence: The later Toulouse sequence and the move to the Roman Missal remain unestablished.

gaps.missing: Original 1516 and 1531 prints; the Soissons missal 'printed shortly after Trent' named in the 1745 letter; dated evidence of the de facto use of the Roman Missal that the letter reports.
gaps.next_source: Gallica/BnF copies of the 1516 and 1531 missals when reachable; Soissons synodal statutes and later-sixteenth-century diocesan editions.
gaps.consequence: The 1745 state is documented without a collated predecessor; the earlier Roman-Missal use is a statement in the 1745 letter, not an independently dated event.

gaps.missing: Inspected later printings, and the Roman restoration act. Ledouble (1880, pp. 383–385, 120) states that the Fitz-James liturgy stayed in use until 1852, that the provincial council of October 1849 decided the return, that the diocesan Proper was approved on 18 July 1851, and that the Roman liturgy was resumed from the first Sunday of Advent 1852 under Bishop de Garsignies. Leclercq de Laprairie (1852, p. 18) says Garsignies had just prescribed it.
gaps.next_source: Garsignies's 1852 mandement and the 1851 Proper; later Soissons printings of the Fitz-James missal.
gaps.consequence: The end of the Fitz-James missal is dated from secondary statements (effective Advent 1852), not from the mandement itself.

gaps.missing: Intervening sixteenth- and seventeenth-century Vienne missals, including the 1676 Villars liturgy the 1849 survey names; an inspected copy of the 1782/1783/1784 provincial missal; the 1822/1840 reprints (the 1849 survey saw a Grenoble 1820 provincial edition); and, after 1801, the Roman restorations in the successor sees (L'épiscopat français p. 263: Grenoble 1869).
gaps.next_source: Gallica bpt6k857944f (1520) and other copies when reachable; originals of the 1784, 1822 and 1840 provincial missals and their mandates.
gaps.consequence: Only one early publication state is documented; the later provincial missal and the Roman adoption remain unestablished.

gaps.missing: Inspected originals of the 1482, 1520 and 1588 missals; Duine's lost 1501 Larchier edition; the eighteenth-century change (the 1849 survey says Nantes preferred the Poitiers liturgy of the Lazarist Jacob at the 1780 Tours provincial assembly, and its table lists Nantes as 'de Poitiers'); the 1837 Missale Nannetense; and the Roman adoption, dated 1858 in a Duine footnote without a mandate date.
gaps.next_source: BnF Rés. B.1814 and BM Nantes 1276/1277 originals; 1837 Merson missal and its mandate; Nantes diocesan mandement of 1858.
gaps.consequence: Two sixteenth-century publication states are documented by scholarly description; the eighteenth- and nineteenth-century states and the Roman adoption remain unverified against books.

gaps.missing: Inspected originals; the undated c.1485 print and the 1500, 1533 and 1557 entries; the 1731 Missale Rhedonense printed at Fougères, which Legg (1881–85, p. 133) lists as Gallican in its colours except black on Good Friday and green as a ferial colour; the 1776/1786 Missale Redonense and 1830/1831 Rhedonense; the 1849 survey's statement that in 1780 the bishop took the Tours liturgy for the cathedral only and kept the Roman liturgy obligatory elsewhere; the named additions that La Borderie says distinguish the 1531 edition from the 1493 text; and the Roman adoption, 1846 (1849 survey p. 381) against 1848 (Duine p. 7 footnote).
gaps.next_source: BnF Vélins 201, Arsenal 2742 and the Grand Séminaire 1588 copy; the 1786 Paris (Michel Lambert) missal and its mandate; the Rennes mandement restoring the Roman liturgy.
gaps.consequence: Four early publication states are documented by scholarly description. The later neo-Gallican and Roman phases remain unestablished, and the adoption year is in conflict.

gaps.missing: Inspected originals of the 1530 (Regnault) and 1535 missals; any later Vannes missal; the eighteenth-century change (Tresvaux, quoted by Duine, dates the adoption of the Paris rite to about 1775; the 1849 survey says Vannes kept its Paris books in 1780; Évenou (2009, p. 519 n. 99) lists 'Vannes 1783' among dioceses that adopted the Paris missal with a Proper of local saints); and the Roman adoption, 1847 (1849 survey p. 381) against 1848 (Duine, Google copy p. 7 = archive.org copy p. 3 note, and p. 114: in 1848 Vannes abandoned the Paris breviary for the Roman liturgy).
gaps.next_source: Gallica bpt6k313781z (1535) when reachable; the Auray 1530 copy; La Borderie's article in the Semaine religieuse du diocèse de Vannes of 3 February 1887; the Vannes mandement restoring the Roman liturgy.
gaps.consequence: One 1535 state is documented from scholarly transcriptions; the Paris-books phase and the Roman adoption remain unverified, with a year conflict.

gaps.period: 1526 to the suppression of the see
gaps.missing: The full colophon text and the referent of 'prefate ecclesie'; any later Léon missal; the 1849 survey's report of the bishop's 1780 refusal of the Tours liturgy ('Nous ne tenons à Rome que par un fil'), which suggests but does not state Roman use. After 1801 the territory belongs to Quimper, where the sources conflict: Duine (archive.org copy p. 3 note) says Bishop de Poulpiquet was introducing the Parisian rite about 1835 and that Quimper rallied to the Roman liturgy in 1852; Bergier (1860, p. 109) says that, by Poulpiquet's circular of 2 December 1844, public office continued with the Roman missal, gradual and vesperal 'as in the past' while the Paris-type breviary was kept, and that by 1846 the clergy had returned to Roman unity.
gaps.next_source: BnF Rés. B.27804 and the Quimper Grand Séminaire copy; Léon synodal statutes; Poulpiquet's circular of 2 December 1844 and the Quimper mandement of 1852.
gaps.consequence: One sixteenth-century state is documented by description; the later Léon liturgy is unestablished.

gaps.missing: Inspected 1488/1496/1548 prints and the title leaf of the 1500 print; the date and instruments of Bishop Jacques Suarez's adoption of the Roman books (Marais and Beaudouin cite Congregation of Rites decrees of 10 May 1608 and 21 March 1676 confirming it); the 1841 Missale Sagiense; and the episcopal ordinance making the Roman liturgy obligatory from 15 May 1864, whose own date is not given (Hommey pp. 409–410; Roman breviary obligatory for new subdeacons from Trinity 1853).
gaps.next_source: Originals of the 1742 and 1841 missals and their mandates; the 1608 and 1676 decrees; Rousselet's 1864 ordinance.
gaps.consequence: The 1500 and 1742 states are documented; the Roman phases on either side of the 1742 book are recorded as dated statements awaiting primary instruments.

gaps.missing: Inspected originals; the catalogue's 1491 entry (no Thérouanne 1491 edition appears in the Saint-Omer bibliography search or Weale's Morinensis entries, while Weale lists a 1491 Arras missal); Weale's 1523 Rouen edition; the use followed in the successor dioceses after the 1559 partition.
gaps.next_source: Saint-Omer and Brussels copies of the 1516/1518/1523 editions; reconcile USUARIUM 87 (1491) against the Arras 1491 missal.
gaps.consequence: Two publication states are documented by description; the route ends with the see (1553/1559) and the 1491 attribution is unverified: neither bibliography searched lists it, and Weale's 1491 Arras missal by Jean du Pré (the printer USUARIUM also names) is a possible confusion to check. This is an inference from silence, not a reattribution.

gaps.missing: Any inspected Saint-Omer missal. The Saint-Omer bibliography (1887) gives only titles: an 1886 pamphlet on the adoption of the Paris breviary in 1747 (p. 77); a 1779 Ordo 'juxta Breviarium ac missale Romanum' issued by Bishop de Bruyères-Chalabre (p. 87), which conflicts with that adoption; and a 1786 Graduale Parisiense (p. 88). Weale–Bohatta (no. 98) list the 1785 Missale Audomarense (Paris, widow Hérissant, quarto; copies Brussels and Lille) without contents. Leroquais's Saint-Omer missal (BM Saint-Omer ms. 60) is the pre-1558 collegiate provost's book, before the see existed. No date of Roman adoption in the successor diocese (Arras) was verified for this route.
gaps.next_source: The Brussels or Lille copy of the 1785 Missale Audomarense and its mandate; the 1886 pamphlet on the 1747 adoption; the 1779 Ordo; Arras diocesan acts.
gaps.consequence: The Saint-Omer route stays without a stage; Paris-type and Roman indications are conflicting titles, not evidence of a book state.

gaps.missing: Inspected originals; the 1492, 1514 and 1533 (Hennequin) editions; the printed form of the 1738 corrections; the 1830 supplement aligning the Bossuet missal with the 1828 breviary (Lalore p. 444); and the Roman restoration. The 1849 survey (p. 346) cites the bishop's mandement of 14 June 1847 and reports three coexisting uses before it (Roman in a third of parishes, Sens in some, Troyes in the rest). The Probationes dossier says 1847 at p. 439, but the Congregation of Rites decree of 6 February 1868 printed at p. 480 says 1846.
gaps.next_source: Originals of the 1580, 1736 and 1830 books; the 14 June 1847 mandement; the 1868 Proprium Missarum approval.
gaps.consequence: The Troyes sequence is documented by description through 1736; the nineteenth-century states rest on dated statements with an unresolved 1846/1847 conflict.

gaps.missing: The catalogue's c.1494 Missale Matisconense (not described in the 1883 Notes); inspected originals; the adoption of the Roman liturgy in 1601 under Gaspard Dinet with a diocesan supplement (the chapter keeping its breviary until 1612), whose extension to the missal is not stated (pp. 143–144); Évenou (2009, p. 519 n. 99) names Mâcon among dioceses that adopted the Paris missal with a Proper of local saints, without a date; and, after Mâcon's absorption into Autun in 1801, the Paris missal (1812), the Missale Aeduense (1831) and the Roman restoration of 1856 (pp. 48–49, 125).
gaps.next_source: An original of the c.1494 and 1532 missals; Dinet's 1601 acts and the Mâcon Officia propria; Autun mandements of 1856.
gaps.consequence: One sixteenth-century state is documented by description; the Roman phase from 1601 and the c.1494 attribution remain unestablished as book states.

gaps.missing: Inspected originals; the 1481 (or c.1492) edition reported via Weale and Calmet; any post-Tridentine Verdun missal. For the catalogue's 1699 Béthune missal, the Pouillé's list of Béthune's liturgical publications (p. 44) names no missal: negative evidence, not proof. The 1779 and 1829 missals were not found. The Pouillé dates the restoration of the Roman liturgy to Bishop Rossat's mandate of 21 February 1862 and circular of 10 June 1862 (p. 55); the 1849 survey's table lists Verdun as Parisian.
gaps.next_source: Originals of the 1554/1557, 1699, 1779 and 1829 missals; Rossat's 1862 mandate.
gaps.consequence: Two sixteenth-century states are documented; the seventeenth- to nineteenth-century sequence is unestablished.

gaps.missing: Inspected originals; L'Huillier's 1492 missal; the 1518 missal (Gallica only); the 1845 reissue; and the Roman adoption. Allou (p. 198) records the Proper approved by the Congregation of Rites on 17 April 1856 and a mandate of 22 August 1858 prescribing the Roman liturgy from the first Sunday of Advent 1858.
gaps.next_source: Gallica bpt6k991401w (1518) and bpt6k56983347 (1709) when reachable; the 22 August 1858 mandate; the 1856 Proper.
gaps.consequence: Meaux states are documented only through Allou's chronicle; the Roman adoption is dated by the chronicle but not checked against the mandate.

gaps.missing: Any inspected Noyon missal: the 1506 Rouen missal (BnF Vélins 171, Gallica only), the Hangest missal of 1541 (title listing, p. 31), the title leaf of the 1631 Sonnius missal, and the title leaf and mandate of the Broglie missal (1770 per Legg and Weale). Ledouble (pp. 383–384) states that the Roman liturgy was reintroduced at Noyon after the council of Reims (1583) and replaced by Bourzac's breviary and missal in 1764, but the bibliography lists only the 1764 breviary. The 1849 survey (pp. 390–391) reports chapter opposition to Bourzac's planned new liturgy in 1763. After 1801, the Noyon liturgy in the Beauvais diocese gave way to the Roman from Pentecost 1857 (mandate of Bishop Gignoux; bibliography p. 31 note).
gaps.next_source: Gallica bpt6k1501962w (1506) when reachable; BL or Amiens copies of the 1631 and 1770 missals (title leaf, Broglie's mandate); Gignoux's 1857 mandate.
gaps.consequence: The 1631 missal (a scholar's negative observation) and the 1770 Broglie missal both stay provisional; the transition between them is not established because Legg's 1631 observation is negative.

gaps.missing: Earlier Sisteron missals; the 1785 mandate; the relation to the 1774 Toulouse missal; the see's suppression in the Revolution and the books later used in its territory.

Rivens.', not examined further); the see's suppression in the Revolution.
